title: Adding JavaScript to a page
learningObjectives: Explain adding javascript to a page and create a small runnable JavaScript example.

understand.concept: JavaScript can be added inline in a script element or loaded from an external file using src. External scripts separate behaviour from markup and can be reused. Script placement and loading attributes affect when code executes relative to document parsing.
understand.whyItMatters: Separating scripts improves organisation and maintainability. Inline event-handler attributes mix behaviour with markup and are generally less maintainable than addEventListener.
understand.analogy: A script element is the doorway that connects a document to JavaScript instructions.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; script loading and JavaScript evaluation follow browser parsing and language rules.

explain.narrative: The script finds the heading and updates its text after the parser has created the element.

examples.explanation: The script finds the heading and updates its text after the parser has created the element.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page or developer console shows the result described in the example.

practise.guidedTask: Move the JavaScript into an external file and load it using a script src attribute. Compare the two approaches.
practise.independentTask: Create a small page with an external or embedded script. Test its execution order and inspect the console for errors.
hints: Keep behaviour separate from semantic markup where practical.
Choose defer, async, or module based on dependencies and ordering.
